name: Return R
idea: A returning foot gives the R a second destination.
type: Compact grotesk; open e, single-storey a, returning R foot.
geometry: 21-unit stem; 19-unit shoulder; open 31-unit counter. The leg returns to a horizontal terminal, rather than ending in a generic diagonal.
limit: The R category is crowded. The returning foot is less apparent at 16px; the master is deliberately simplified there.
small: The 16px cut thickens the counter floor and widens its opening. The returning foot becomes a square hook; no rounded subpixel tip.

name: Held quotation
idea: Two spoken fragments settle onto a single retained line.
type: Soft humanist lettering; wider apertures and a short-footed R.
geometry: Two offset quotation forms and a retained baseline. The second tail ends above the baseline, leaving an intentional open interval.
limit: Quotation marks are familiar editorial material. Recognition depends on the retained baseline, not on quotation marks alone.
small: The 16px cut removes the second tail curve and opens the gap above the baseline to 2px. Both quote heads remain 4px wide.

name: Retrace
idea: One path moves forward, turns back and continues.
type: Square-shouldered grotesk; clipped e aperture and firm horizontal rhythm.
geometry: A single filled contour with two opposing right-angle returns. A 20-unit channel separates the passes; no arrowhead, loop or implied playback button.
limit: Can be read as a numeral 2, an abstract S or a route. Its angularity is more technical than conversational and needs the warmer wordmark beside it.
small: The 16px cut uses a 3px band and a minimum 1px channel, aligned to a 16px grid. At 32px it uses the fuller master proportions.

name: Margin ligature
idea: Recallo’s double l becomes a shared editorial margin.
type: Original low-contrast serif lettering, linked l feet and a crisp R leg.
geometry: Two ascenders share a stepped foot. Small head serifs distinguish the stems; the lower rail continues the wordmark’s reading baseline.
limit: The wordmark carries this route. In isolation the symbol may read as II or a small architectural monogram; weaker in a crowded app grid.
small: Serifs widen to full pixels at 16px; the shared foot is 2–3px deep. Use the serif master from 32px upward, not a scaled full wordmark.

name: Binding fold
idea: A loose strip folds into a bound, retained edge.
type: Expanded lettering with an upright R and broad, quiet rounded counters.
geometry: A vertical spine supports a rising flap and a separated lower fold. The diagonal seam is structural and remains open in one color.
limit: A folded-strip reading needs introduction; some viewers may see a flag or K. Avoid adding more folds or trying to hide another letter.
small: The 16px cut makes the fold seam at least 1px, widens the spine to 4px and squares the lower flap. No decorative crease line is used.
